rationale: The buyer is a paying LLM API user — developer or solo operator running agentic workflows — who already has a budget (Anthropic/OpenAI API spend) and experiences concrete productivity losses when model performance degrades; this is a real, recurring pain with daily/near-daily frequency. A model performance monitoring and alerting service is genuinely buildable: Claude can run standardized benchmark prompts on a schedule, store results, detect regressions, and email/webhook alerts — no custom ML, no compliance moat needed. Operational autonomy scores 8 because once configured, the service runs and alerts hands-off. The validation gate to clear is confirming developers will pay ($10–$30/mo) rather than self-build — that's the key unknown.
solution_plan: (1) WHAT: A subscription alert service that runs standardized benchmark tasks against one or more LLM APIs on a fixed schedule (e.g., every 6 hours) and notifies the subscriber when performance regresses beyond a threshold. (2) BUILD: The factory builds a Claude-orchestrated benchmark runner — a set of canonical prompt tasks scored automatically, results stored in a simple DB, regression detection logic, and email/webhook alert delivery — plus a landing page and Stripe subscription link ($19/mo); no coding by Youval. (3) SELL: Outreach to developers in LLM-focused communities (HN, r/LocalLLaMA, Anthropic Discord, OpenAI forums) who are already complaining about model degradation — Youval approves each outreach batch before it goes out. (4) MAINTAIN: Benchmark runs, scoring, alerting, and billing all run autonomously via Claude + this codebase; Youval's only recurring touch is approving new outreach batches and reviewing the weekly summary. The key validation question: will developers pay $19/mo or self-build a cron job? Run a 2-week pre-sell to 50 targets before building.
notes: All build gates met at current scores (operational_autonomy=8≥7, buildability_with_ai=7≥6, buyer_clarity=7≥6, willingness_to_pay=6≥5). Stage is validate rather than build because responsiveness_signal=2 (no test data yet) and the total sits exactly at the build threshold — confirm payment intent before committing build resources.
